result.output:
**Formats:** You can request one or more of these:

- `markdown`, `summary`, `html` (cleaned), `rawHtml` (unmodified)
- `rawBase64` (must be the only format requested)
- `screenshot` (with options like `fullPage`, `quality`, `viewport`)
- `links`, `images`, `branding`, `product`
- `json` (structured output, with a schema or a prompt)
- `audio` and `video` (for supported video URLs such as YouTube)
- `question` and `highlights` (answers and source text, returned in `answer` and `highlights`)
- `query` (with `prompt` and optional `mode`)

**Response shape:** The response has `success` and `data`. Output keys match the formats you choose. For example:

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "markdown": "...",
    "html": "...",
    "metadata": {
      "title": "...",
      "description": "...",
      "language": "en",
      "sourceURL": "...",
      "statusCode": 200,
      "contentType": "text/html"
    }
  }
}
```

`metadata` also includes Open Graph fields. `statusCode` is the page's HTTP status, separate from the API's own status. Routed URLs also include `metadata.provider`. The document doesn't show the exact output shape for `links`.

**Unsupported or blocked sites:** The document doesn't list blocked sites or mention social media in general. It does say that LinkedIn profile and company pages aren't scraped by Firecrawl: "Firecrawl doesn't scrape LinkedIn." Instead, third-party providers answer those URLs. Sub-pages such as `/in/<handle>/details/experience` fail with `THIRD_PARTY_DATA_UNSUPPORTED_URL` (400). If enrichment is off, the request fails with `THIRD_PARTY_DATA_ENRICHMENT_NOT_ENABLED` (403).

content.text:
I couldn't confirm that Firecrawl works on TikTok, and the evidence points against it. A Firecrawl MCP server isn't connected in this session, so I couldn't test it. Everything below comes from the docs and third-party reports.

**TikTok support**
- Firecrawl's official docs don't list blocked sites. The only exclusion they name is LinkedIn, which they hand to third-party providers.
- Two third-party write-ups say Firecrawl refuses Instagram, YouTube and TikTok URLs. The error tells you to contact support to enable the site on your account. Both posts come from ScrapeCreators, which sells a competing social-media scraper, so they are biased.
- Those reports are at least partly out of date for YouTube. The current docs show `audio` and `video` formats demonstrated on YouTube. They describe the source as "supported video URLs" without listing which sites those are, and TikTok isn't mentioned anywhere.

The only way to settle it is to send one request with a TikTok URL and see whether it comes back with content or the "not supported" error.

**What a scrape returns**

You choose formats per request, and the response is `{ success, data }`. `data` has one key per requested format plus `metadata`:

- `markdown`, `summary`, `html` (cleaned), `rawHtml`, `rawBase64`
- `screenshot`, `links`, `images`, `branding`, `product`
- `json`: structured extraction from a schema or a prompt
- `audio` / `video`: a signed Google Cloud Storage URL to an MP3 or the best-quality video, which expires after 1 hour
- `question` / `highlights` / `query`: answers to a prompt about the page
- `metadata`: title, description, language, `sourceURL`, `statusCode` (the page's own HTTP status), `contentType` and Open Graph fields

For nagara, a TikTok page would mostly scrape to a thin shell: a caption, hashtags and the OG description. The real content is the video's speech. If the `audio` format does work for TikTok, it would give you an MP3, and you would still have to transcribe it yourself.

If you have a Firecrawl API key, I can run a curl request against a TikTok URL to check what comes back.

Sources:
- [Firecrawl docs: Scrape](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/scrape)
- [Firecrawl docs: Scrape API reference](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/api-reference/endpoint/scrape)

Firecrawl doesn't support TikTok. I used the dev key from `pipeline/.dev.vars` to scrape a TikTok video and a TikTok profile. Every request was refused before any scraping happened, whether it asked for markdown only or for markdown plus audio:

```json
{
  "success": false,
  "error": "We apologize for the inconvenience but we do not support this site. If you are part of an enterprise and want to have a further conversation about this, please contact our sales team here: https://www.firecrawl.dev/contact-sales"
}
```

No markdown, metadata or audio comes back. Only an enterprise agreement with their sales team would lift the block. I didn't record the HTTP status code. Since `success` is false, nagara's client in `pipeline/src/firecrawl/client.ts` would most likely throw `firecrawl answered <status>` on a TikTok URL, and the item would fail in the fetch step.

To get TikTok into nagara you'd need a different source, such as a TikTok-specific scraper API or yt-dlp to pull the audio, followed by speech-to-text to get the transcript.

content.text:
yt-dlp works on TikTok with no API key. On the test video it returned the metadata (caption, uploader, a 10 s duration, the sound's name) and downloaded two files to `/tmp/tmp.o0qZg13bYC/`:

- **`track.mp3`** comes from the `audio` format. It is the TikTok "sound" attached to the post, which here is "original sound" by "tiff", so it matches the video. On posts that use a licensed song it will be the song, not what the person says.
- **`video.mp3`** is the audio pulled out of the mp4, which is always what the video actually plays. If we use yt-dlp, this is the file to take.

What I found:

- **No subtitles:** this video has neither manual subtitles nor auto-captions. TikTok does auto-caption many newer videos with speech, and yt-dlp exposes those as `subtitles`. When they exist, they are a free transcript and we'd skip speech-to-text.
- **Impersonation warning:** yt-dlp warned that it had no browser-impersonation target installed (`curl_cffi`). It worked anyway this time, but TikTok blocks it intermittently without one.
- **Can't run on Workers:** yt-dlp is a Python CLI with ffmpeg, so a Worker can't run it. It would have to run on Modal next to `tts/`, or as a new service.

This test video is a dog with music, so it says nothing about transcripts. Send me a TikTok URL where someone is talking and I'll check whether it has captions. If it doesn't, I can transcribe the audio locally with Whisper to see what quality we'd get.
did it download the video too?

It downloaded the video but didn't keep it. To get `video.mp3`, yt-dlp fetched the 540p mp4, extracted the audio with ffmpeg, and then deleted the mp4, which is what `-x` does unless you add `-k`. The directory listing confirms only `track.mp3`, `video.mp3`, `info.json` and `err.txt` are left.

If we only need the audio, there's no way to avoid downloading the video. Except for the separate `audio` track, every TikTok format is a combined mp4, so we have to fetch the whole file to get the speech. For short TikToks that's only a few MB per item.
